title: Rhythm Club, learning English and being told to build volume
summary: Without English he hangs out at the Rhythm Club, plays his sax, is told he needs more volume, and names the musicians who gathered there.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I sat. I couldn't speak no English, but I used to go around the RHYTHM Club around the corner on 131st, and I used to go there every night, order me seats and hang around there. And they come in there, all the corner musicians, all the guys, you see, and if I come in there, you know, I had a hell of a time to -- to transmit myself to that.

But I mean, they just like a light, they had to lighten me. So I used to bring my saxophone around and play. You know what I mean. They -- and then a whole lot of those guys said, 'You play beautiful. You play beautiful saxophone.' The only thing, you got to develop more volume, because, you know, down there in Cuba they play soft music, you know.
And those great, big, heavy bands here, they would drown me. So --
Who were you -- who were you hanging out with?

Well, in those days the guys that hang around there were all like guys like Benny Carter, Jimmy Harrison, Red Allen, Lou Metcalf, Charlie Johnson, the Whitman brothers -- that used to play with Charlie Johnson -- Wilbur de Paris, Sidney de Paris, all the big musicians in those days, all the jazz musicians, all the guys from Procope, Johnny, from Fletcher Henderson, Jeffrey, Bozobelli (phonetic), all the biggest guys.

I was -- hang around all day, and before I knew, I was speaking English. That I do know, because when -- no way for me to speak Spanish then. No Spanish people around here. You can hardly see one. So I have to either talk English or die.
